parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReceivingService is an application/domain service that orchestrates domain objects. Its own logic is business logic: it validates the received quantity, decides how much to take from each bin when picking, and asks Item.needsReorder whether to reorder. It contains no SQL, schema, transaction, connection, HTTP or framework code. It only calls find, holding and store on the injected tables. Depending on persistence tables is an import-direction matter, which is out of scope. Two points are borderline. First, the private item()/bin() helpers and the pick loop rebuild Item/Bin from table rows, and { ...bin } turns them back into plain objects to save. This conversion would normally sit in a repository, but here it is a few lines of glue with no storage logic. Second, PickContextDto carries an unused requestId. It is a type with no behaviour, not transport handling. Neither amounts to a misplaced responsibility under the rubric.
